quotes.text: I wanna be in the studio, but you have to sell the records, so you have to go do some shows. Shows I can take 'em or leave 'em. I'm a studio dude. My main love is being in the studio. I like to make music 24 hours a day.

I'm a background type of dude. I'm not like a dude that likes to be up front where people are all looking at me. I'm a shy dude; I be in the background making my beats, you know what I'm sayin'? Chillin'.
It was all like at once. Like I do Dudley Perkins one day, then the next day be Madvillain and so on. That's how I always work. Ten projects at once.
I don't think about it. I just do the music. I don't think about it how other people think; it just happens. I get bored, so I gotta move to something else. I get bored easy.
The reason why I collaborate with MCs is that I wanna see if my style can fit with theirs or vice versa. See if we can bring something together. With anybody. I collaborate with anybody who is dope.
Just be dope. And have some money. Be dope. That's all: just be dope. Have an open, creative mind.

When we were doing Madvillain, we were supposed to do one song. It turned into a whole album, cause he liked the music so much. We were just trying to work on, see if we can do a song together and it turned into a whole album.

I trusted him on that. He's one of my favorite lyricists. So I trusted him already. And shit came out crazy. I trust everybody I work with, I don't have to tell things. We trust each other. Just connect without sayin' and shit, you know what I'm sayin'? There's only certain people that you can do that with.
I did half of it. My brother Oh No did the other half.
We used to live together. And I had my equipment there. When I left, he could do his thing, you know?
I was makin' beats. I leave to Brazil next week. I gonna be making beats. Just going out there on a vacation and just make beats.
Yeah, some records. That's where Hip-Hop is from anyway: Records and sampling. That's what I do, you know what I'm sayin'?

Usually I bring my stuff anywhere. I didn't bring it this time, but I'm bringing my stuff everywhere, you know what I'm sayin'? If I have time for that long enough, I bring all my equipment and buy records at a store. Make some beats.
The studio's very basic.
Madlib is part of the reason I make music
A lot of voice notes and mumbles. Eventually the lyrics start to form. Kind of magical that something literally comes from nothing. Seeing the process is wild.

There was always a natural ability with music for me. A chance for me to tap into my inner child. I wasn't amazing with fashion especially pattern cutting and I remember the competition always being intense lol so I've always found it more enjoyable just living in my own music bubble.

It's always important to embrace/acknowledge where you came from. SoundCloud was such an amazing period for me. It was raw, no one cared how rough the track sounded as long as it had the 'vibe'. Millionaire was one of my most played tracks at the time so it just felt natural to reintroduce it.

I've always enjoyed the challenge of creating and making something that already exists and sounds brand new, and I think making songs that I really love my own and dissecting it by resigning the lyrics is just a really great experience. Just to see how a song was written and especially with this song, just talking about not being satisfied with having money, reaching the pinnacle of being a millionaire, but still feeling so empty. I think the subject speaks for today's society the things that we were told to chase, all of the vanity of fame then when you suddenly get it and it's actually not what it seemed and you feel empty/ unfulfilled. It's quite a deep song.

I think this time around, I've been really playful and kind of reconnected with my inner child. It's so beautiful because I think making the sound is an achievement in itself so this time around I'm really just letting myself be free and not really think about the end product too much, and be more in the moment.

So sick! I think there are a lot of sides to me that people still don't know that I'm still discovering. One of the sides of my foundation is hip-hop, Madlib is part of the reason why I make music. He is a a legend in the game, so having the chance to express myself over his music was phenomenal.
